biography: Alister McRae, a name synonymous with raw talent and audacious driving, hails from the rugged landscapes of Scotland. From a young age, the roar of engines was his lullaby, his father a local rally enthusiast who instilled in him a love for speed and a devil-may-care attitude. His entry into professional racing was almost accidental; substituting for an injured driver in a local rallycross event, he stunned everyone with his aggressive style and uncanny car control, securing a podium finish. This unexpected success launched his career, quickly attracting the attention of VW Polo RX. A defining moment came at the 2022 World RX of Norway, where, despite a damaged suspension, he fought tooth and nail, eventually snatching victory in the final lap. Now at 32, McRae is considered to be at his peak, a force to be reckoned with on the rallycross circuit, his flashy persona as captivating as his driving.
drivingStyle: McRae's driving style can be best described as controlled chaos. He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the car to its absolute limit. Tire management isn't exactly his forte, preferring to attack from the outset, relying on raw pace to gain an advantage. He thrives under pressure, often performing best when the stakes are highest, a trait that makes him a formidable opponent in head-to-head battles.

rivalries.name: Marco Venturi
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at the 2021 Swedish RX, where Venturi accused McRae of deliberately blocking him.

rivalries.name: Ingrid Bergman
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities both on and off the track. Bergman, known for her calculated approach, often clashes with McRae's flamboyant style.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A rivalry born from several close finishes, with Tanaka consistently challenging McRae for podium positions.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky blue wristband given to him by his sister before every race.
Listens to heavy metal music at full volume right before getting into the car to get 'pumped up'.
Refuses to walk under any ladders, even inside the paddock.
famousQuote: "If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 World RX of Norway after battling through a damaged suspension, showcasing his determination and skill.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2020 World RX final in South Africa while leading, costing him a potential championship title.
